set.body:
# Representation

Authority: PRD.json 0.1.0, release target 1.0.

## Objective
Implement the proven storage, dtype, shape, layout, rank, construction, indexing, and reference-model foundations.

## Product requirements

## RAV-REP-001 [must]
Every array shall use one flat buffer plus immutable shape, strides, and offset metadata.

Acceptance:
- No core representation uses nested arrays or nested collections.
- A slow reference accessor and optimized accessors return the same value for every valid logical index.

## RAV-LAY-001 [must]
Shape products, canonical strides, offset transformations, axis coalescing, and reachable-address bounds shall use Long intermediates and checked narrowing to Int.

Acceptance:
- Overflow is rejected instead of wrapped.
- A zero-sized shape such as (0, Int.MaxValue, Int.MaxValue) cannot silently overflow while constructing nominally unused strides.
- Every accepted nonempty layout maps its complete logical domain inside the backing buffer.

## RAV-LAY-002 [must]
Layout.offset shall always denote the physical address of logical index zero.

Acceptance:
- A view operation adjusts offset when introducing a negative stride.
- The loop planner does not normalize an already adjusted negative-stride offset a second time.
- Double reversal restores the original logical values and layout mapping.

## RAV-LAY-003 [must]
Read-only layouts shall support positive strides, negative strides, zero strides, nonzero offsets, rank-zero arrays, and zero-length axes.

Acceptance:
- Generated tests cover each layout form and their compositions.
- HasBroadcastStride is set only for a zero-stride axis whose logical length is greater than one.

## RAV-RANK-001 [must]
Constructors with statically known arity shall infer Rank[N], while dynamic shape constructors shall return AnyRank.

Acceptance:
- NDArray.zeros[Double](3, 4) has type Array2[Double].
- Shape.from returns a dynamic-rank Shape through a validating boundary.
- requireRank[N] returns Either[RankMismatch, NDArray[A, Rank[N]]].

## RAV-RANK-002 [must]
Rank-lowering operations shall reject statically known Rank[0] and validate positive dynamic rank.

Acceptance:
- select, squeeze, and single-axis rank-lowering reductions do not compile for Rank[0].
- The corresponding operation on AnyRank fails with a precise runtime error when the actual rank is zero.
- No public operation produces Rank[-1].

## RAV-DTYPE-001 [must]
Ravel 1.0 shall expose a closed primitive dtype family consisting of Boolean, Byte, Short, Int, Long, Float, and Double.

Acceptance:
- Every supported dtype has a known physical representation and cross-platform copy semantics.
- Boolean supports storage and elementwise equality but no numeric cast.
- Byte and Short support storage, casts, ordering, comparisons, min, max, argMin, and argMax, but not pointwise arithmetic, sum, or product.
- Int, Long, Float, and Double support same-dtype arithmetic.

## RAV-DTYPE-002 [must]
Binary arithmetic shall require equal operand dtypes in 1.0.

Acceptance:
- NDArray[Int] plus NDArray[Int] compiles.
- NDArray[Int] plus NDArray[Double] does not compile.
- NDArray[Byte] plus NDArray[Byte] does not compile.
- Users can opt into a different dtype with an explicit cast.

## RAV-DTYPE-003 [must]
Numeric cast behavior shall follow one documented conversion table on the JVM and Scala.js.

Acceptance:
- Integral widening is exact where the target can represent every source value.
- Integral narrowing retains low-order bits with signed two's-complement interpretation.
- Integral-to-floating conversion uses IEEE rounding and may lose precision.
- Float-to-Double is exact; Double-to-Float uses IEEE rounding, preserves signed zero, maps overflow to infinity, and preserves NaN classification without guaranteeing its payload.
- Floating-to-Int or Long truncates toward zero, maps NaN to zero, and clamps infinities and finite out-of-range values.
- Floating-to-Byte or Short applies the Int conversion followed by integral narrowing.
- Cross-platform edge-case tests cover extrema, representability boundaries, infinities, NaNs, and signed zeros.

## RAV-DTYPE-004 [must]
Integral arithmetic shall use fixed-width Scala semantics, and floating arithmetic shall use IEEE 754 semantics.

Acceptance:
- Int and Long overflow wraps.
- Integral division by zero fails.
- Documented edge cases such as abs(Int.MinValue) match the corresponding Scala primitive operation.
- JVM and Scala.js parity tests cover the agreed behavior.

## RAV-OWN-001 [must]
Normal public constructors shall copy input storage and return owned immutable NDArray values.

Acceptance:
- Changing the caller's original array after construction does not change the NDArray.
- NDArray exposes no update method.
- Owned NDArray does not expose its mutable backing array or typed array zero-copy.

## RAV-API-001 [must]
Public indexing shall provide direct rank-one through rank-four overloads plus an arbitrary-rank fallback.

Acceptance:
- apply overloads validate each index.
- at(IArray[Int]) validates index rank and bounds.
- Physical offset calculations use Long intermediates before checked narrowing.
- Validated internal loop plans may use unchecked buffer access without repeating operand bounds checks per element.

## RAV-API-002 [must]
NDArray shall not extend IndexedSeq, Iterable, or another standard Scala collection abstraction.

Acceptance:
- Traversal is available through explicitly named foreachElement, elementsIterator, and foreachIndex operations.
- No inherited collection builder can silently discard shape.

## RAV-ERR-001 [must]
Deterministic programming errors in ordinary numerical expressions shall throw precise sealed NDArrayException subtypes.

Acceptance:
- The error family includes ShapeMismatch, BroadcastMismatch, InvalidAxis, InvalidShape, InvalidSlice, LayoutOverflow, NonContiguousLayout, and EmptyReduction.
- Boundary parsers and refinements such as Shape.from, Slice.from, requireRank, and external parsing may return Either.
- BroadcastMismatch reports both shapes and the first incompatible aligned axis.

## Deliverables
- DType capability hierarchy and complete cast contract.
- Dtype-specific Data variants and platform buffers.
- Shape and checked Layout.
- CanDropAxis and requireRank.
- Immutable constructors and indexing overloads.
- Slow reference iterator.

## Exit criteria
- Cross-platform cast edge tests pass.
- Layout overflow tests include zero-sized stride overflow.
- Negative-stride offset tests pass.
- Rank-zero operations cannot produce negative rank.

## Required law coverage
ShapeLaws, LayoutLaws, DTypeLaws, CastLaws, and the representation portion of KernelLaws.

## Relevant risks
RISK-003. Preserve the Phase 0 raw-buffer ABI and no-aliasing guarantee.

## Completion rule
Close this epic only when every listed requirement and exit criterion has executable evidence on every promised platform. Record implementation commits, tests, compiler-output evidence, and any accepted deviation in mote notes.
set.title: EPIC P1: Build checked representation, dtype, and rank contracts
